definitionEn: to criticise someone or something strongly and publicly
senseNote: Здесь — публично осуждать. Реже denounce значит «донести на кого-то» или «денонсировать договор».
situation: A leader, group or public figure says openly that an action, law or person is wrong or shameful.

examples.text: Human rights groups [[denounced]] the new law as an attack on free speech.
In an angry post, the footballer [[denounced]] the racist abuse he had received after the match.
Two senior surgeons publicly [[denounced]] the plan to cut night staff, calling it dangerous.

texts: It is easy to [[denounce]] greed while quietly enjoying its benefits.
The minister was forced to [[denounce]] the comments made by his own adviser.
Few writers dared to [[denounce]] the regime while it was still in power.

badCollocation.text: [[denounce]] someone to five years in prison
badCollocation.noteRu: Суд приговаривает — sentence someone to five years. Denounce — публично осуждать, а не выносить приговор.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Denounce someone as a traitor — публично заклеймить предателем. Accuse требует of (accuse of treason), blame — for, а betray значит «предать».

nuance.text: The charity [[denounced]] the company's treatment of its workers as shameful.
nuance.explanationRu: Denounce — публично осуждать чужие действия. Renounce — официально отказываться от своего: титула, гражданства, убеждений.

reverse.text: He [[renounced]] his citizenship and moved abroad for good.
reverse.explanationRu: От гражданства, титула или наследства отказываются: renounce. Denounce — осуждать, а не отказываться.

fixIt.text: Several MPs publicly [[judged]] the decision to close the children's hospital.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Публично осудить» решение — denounce (или condemn). Judge — «оценивать, судить», осуждения в нём нет.

wordFormation.text: The report ends with a fierce [[denunciation]] of the way refugees are treated.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Did you see what the mayor said about the graffiti on the war memorial?"
options: Yes, he denounced that the memorial will be cleaned by Friday.
Yeah, he denounced it as a disgrace, and fair enough, really.
Indeed. I hereby formally denounce the aforementioned graffiti.
reply.explanationRu: Denounce something as a disgrace — публично осудить, как мэр осудил вандализм. «Denounced that» в значении «объявил» — ошибка (нужно announced), а третий ответ звучит как официальный документ.

definitionEn: packed with complex ideas or information and therefore hard to understand
senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — густой, плотный: dense fog, a dense forest. Здесь — о тексте, перегруженном сложными идеями.
situation: You describe a book, report or lecture that contains so many difficult ideas that it is slow and tiring to get through.

examples.text: The first chapter is so [[dense]] that I had to read every paragraph twice.
The contract is written in [[dense]] legal language that most clients never read properly.
The novel is beautiful but [[dense]], so it's not one to read on the beach.

texts: His prose is [[dense]] but rewarding if you take your time.
The slides were too [[dense]] to read from the back of the room.
Academic writing does not have to be [[dense]] to be serious.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Плотный график» — a busy, tight или packed schedule. Dense так не говорят: это о тексте, лесе или тумане.

collocationTask.prompt: The article is ___ with technical terms.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Dense with — о тексте, где очень много терминов или идей. Full требует of (full of terms), а busy и tight с текстом так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: This paper is far too [[dense]] for first-year students to follow.
nuance.explanationRu: Dense о тексте — насыщенный сложными идеями, трудный для понимания. Thick о книге — просто толстая, со множеством страниц; сложность текста так не описывают.

fixIt.text: The lecture was so [[saturated]] that I couldn't follow the main argument.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Насыщенная» лекция — dense. Saturated — «пропитанный влагой» или «перенасыщенный» (о рынке), к лекции не подходит.

wordFormation.text: The book is so [[densely]] written that even experts read it slowly.

reply.context: A classmate asks: "Is the book on the reading list worth starting this weekend?"
options: It's quite dense, so you'll probably finish it in an hour.
Its prose is of considerable density; weekend perusal is inadvisable.
It's brilliant but pretty dense, so give yourself a few quiet evenings.
reply.explanationRu: Dense — трудный для чтения из-за обилия идей, поэтому нужно время. Прочитать такую книгу за час — противоречие, а второй ответ слишком книжный для разговора.

definitionEn: how many people or things there are in an area of a given size
senseNote: Здесь — плотность населения, застройки, пикселей. В физике density — плотность вещества (масса на единицу объёма).
situation: You compare how crowded cities or regions are by counting people or buildings per square kilometre.

examples.text: The island has one of the highest population [[densities]] in Europe.
Planners want to increase housing [[density]] near train stations instead of building on farmland.
The new phone screen has a higher pixel [[density]], so photos look much sharper.

texts: Traffic [[density]] peaks between eight and nine in the morning.
The city's [[density]] makes public transport cheap to run.
Areas of low [[density]] are expensive to serve by bus.

badCollocation.noteRu: Плотность бывает high или low, а не big или small: a high population density.

collocationTask.explanationRu: О плотности говорят high или low: a high population density. Big, strong и wide с density не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The city has a population [[density]] of 8,000 people per square kilometre.
nuance.explanationRu: Показатель «сколько людей на квадратный километр» — density. Concentration — скопление в одном месте: a concentration of shops in the centre.

reverse.text: There is a large [[concentration]] of tourists around the cathedral.
reverse.explanationRu: Скопление людей в одном месте — concentration. Density — показатель на единицу площади, и large density не говорят.

fixIt.text: This district has the highest population [[thickness]] in the country, so parking is a nightmare.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Плотность населения» — population density. Thickness — толщина предмета (стены, льда), к населению не подходит.

wordFormation.text: The high [[density]] of housing here leaves little room for parks.

rewrite.original: An enormous number of people live in every square kilometre of the city.
rewrite.frame: The city has an extremely high ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Число жителей на единицу площади — population density.

definitionEn: the state of needing someone or something so much that you cannot manage without them
situation: A country, company or person cannot manage without the money, help or supplies that someone else provides.

examples.text: The country is trying to reduce its [[dependence]] on imported gas.
Nicotine creates a strong physical [[dependence]], which is why quitting is so hard.
Moving abroad forced her to overcome her [[dependence]] on her parents for every decision.

texts: Too much [[dependence]] on spellcheckers can weaken your writing skills.
Bad harvests exposed the region's [[dependence]] on imported grain.
The start-up's [[dependence]] on a single investor worried its staff.

badCollocation.noteRu: После dependence нужен предлог on: dependence on parents. «From» — калька с «зависимость от».

collocationTask.explanationRu: С предлогом on сочетается dependence (или reliance). Addiction и attachment требуют to, а confidence — in.

nuance.text: Young children's [[dependence]] on their parents is completely natural.
nuance.explanationRu: Dependence — естественная потребность в ком-то: дети в родителях, страна в импорте. Addiction — болезненное пристрастие к наркотикам или играм; о детях звучит абсурдно.

reverse.text: Her [[addiction]] to online shopping left her deep in debt.
reverse.explanationRu: Пагубная страсть к шопингу, играм или телефону — addiction to. Dependence звучит здесь слишком нейтрально, и предлог to с ним не используется.

fixIt.text: The region's [[reliability]] on tourism made the pandemic especially painful.
fixIt.explanationRu: Reliability — надёжность. «Зависимость от туризма» — dependence (или reliance) on tourism.

wordFormation.text: Many small towns have an unhealthy [[dependence]] on a single employer.

reply.context: Your manager asks: "Seventy per cent of our income comes from one client. Should we worry?"
options: Yes, that kind of dependence on one client is risky if they ever leave.
Not really, our dependence means we're free to choose any client we like.
Totally, mate, the whole dependence thing is well dodgy.
reply.explanationRu: Dependence on one client — зависимость от одного клиента, и это риск. Во втором ответе dependence перепутано с independence, а третий слишком фамильярен для разговора с руководителем.

definitionEn: to represent or show someone or something in art, film or writing
situation: A painting, novel or film shows people, places or events in a particular way.

examples.text: The mural [[depicts]] fishermen bringing in their catch at dawn.
Early novels often [[depicted]] city life as dirty and dangerous.
In the advert, the bank is [[depicted]] as a friendly neighbour who is always there to help.

texts: It is hard to [[depict]] grief without becoming sentimental.
The game's designers wanted to [[depict]] the city exactly as it looked in 1920.
Children were asked to [[depict]] their family using only three colours.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Изобразить удивление» (притвориться) — pretend to be surprised или fake surprise. Depict — изображать в картине, фильме или книге.

collocationTask.prompt: The film ___ him as a lonely genius.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Depict somebody as something — изображать кого-то каким-то в фильме или книге. Draw — рисовать, outline — кратко излагать, а images как глагол здесь не подходит.

nuance.text: The documentary [[depicts]] daily life on a remote Scottish island.
nuance.explanationRu: Depict — изображать в фильме, книге, на картине. Picture (глагол) — представлять себе в воображении: I can't picture him as a boss.

reverse.text: I can't [[picture]] myself living in such a big city.
reverse.explanationRu: «Представить себя» в воображении — picture yourself. Depict — изображать в произведении, а не мысленно.

fixIt.text: The fresco on the ceiling [[describes]] scenes from the life of a local saint.
fixIt.explanationRu: Describe — рассказывать словами. Фреска или картина изображает: depicts.

wordFormation.text: Critics praised the film's honest [[depiction]] of life in a care home.

rewrite.original: In the film, the town is shown as a dangerous place.
rewrite.explanationRu: Конструкция depict something as something — изображать что-то каким-то.

definitionEn: to move soldiers, police or equipment into position so that they are ready to act
senseNote: В IT deploy значит «выкатывать, запускать» программу; здесь — о войсках, полиции и спасателях.
situation: Soldiers, police officers or rescue teams are sent to an area and put in position, ready for action.

examples.text: Hundreds of extra police officers were [[deployed]] in the city centre for the final.
Within hours of the earthquake, the government [[deployed]] rescue teams with sniffer dogs.
Around two thousand troops will be [[deployed]] to the region as part of the peace mission.

texts: The government may [[deploy]] the army if the floods get worse.
Mountain rescue services now [[deploy]] drones to search for missing hikers.
It takes about ten minutes to [[deploy]] the flood barriers.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Развернуть дискуссию» — start или open a debate. Deploy — развернуть войска, полицию или технику.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Войска на границу направляют: deploy (или send) troops to the border. Place и put требуют at или on, а locate значит «найти» или «располагать».

nuance.text: The navy [[deployed]] two ships to protect the fishing fleet.
nuance.explanationRu: Оба глагола переводятся «развернуть», но deploy — направить силы или технику на позицию, а unfold — развернуть что-то сложенное: карту, письмо, одеяло.

reverse.text: She [[unfolded]] the letter and began to read.
reverse.explanationRu: Развернуть сложенный лист, карту или скатерть — unfold. Deploy — только о войсках, полиции и технике.

fixIt.text: The government has [[located]] two thousand extra troops along the border.
fixIt.explanationRu: Разместить войска — deploy (или station) troops. Locate значит «найти» или «располагать» (здание), а не перебрасывать силы.

reply.context: In a planning meeting for a big outdoor concert, the event manager asks: "How are we handling security at the gates?"
options: We'll deploy the fans at each gate so they can find their seats faster.
Security personnel shall be deployed in accordance with the aforementioned protocols.
We'll deploy extra stewards at every gate as soon as the crowds start arriving.
reply.explanationRu: Deploy stewards — расставить охрану по местам, это верно. Зрителей не deploy, их пропускают, а второй ответ звучит как канцелярский документ, а не реплика на совещании.

definitionEn: the process of putting new technology or systems into use on a large scale
senseNote: Также — развёртывание войск (troop deployment); здесь — внедрение технологий, сетей и систем.
situation: A company or government starts using new equipment or software widely, for example across a whole country.

examples.text: The [[deployment]] of faster mobile networks has been slow in rural areas.
Cheaper batteries could speed up the [[deployment]] of solar power in poorer countries.
After a smooth [[deployment]], all staff were using the new booking system within a week.

texts: Large-scale [[deployment]] of the software begins in March.
Wind farm [[deployment]] has doubled in the past five years.
The app's [[deployment]] was delayed by a last-minute security bug.

badCollocation.noteRu: Новый закон или правила вводят: the introduction of a new law. Deployment — внедрение техники, сетей и программ.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Внедрение техники — deployment. Placement — размещение (стажёра, рекламы), occupation — профессия или оккупация, appointment — назначение или встреча.

nuance.text: The [[deployment]] of charging stations along motorways is behind schedule.
nuance.explanationRu: Implementation — выполнение плана, решения или закона. Deployment — физическое внедрение техники: станций, сетей, дронов.

reverse.text: The [[implementation]] of the peace agreement will take years.
reverse.explanationRu: Соглашение, реформу или решение выполняют: implementation. Deployment — про технику и системы, а не про договорённости.

fixIt.text: The [[implantation]] of AI tools in our hospitals is happening faster than expected.
fixIt.explanationRu: Внедрение технологий — deployment (или introduction). Implantation — имплантация в медицине, к программам и системам не подходит.

wordFormation.text: Engineers are preparing for the nationwide [[deployment]] of the new payment system.

rewrite.original: The company started using the new software in all its offices in June.
rewrite.frame: The ____ the new software in all offices began in June.
rewrite.explanationRu: После deployment нужен предлог of: the deployment of the software.

definitionEn: to leave a layer of sand, mud or minerals on something, as water does
senseNote: Базовое значение (B2) — класть деньги на счёт. Здесь — о реке, воде, ветре: оставлять слой ила, песка, осадка.
situation: A river, flood or hard water leaves behind a layer of mud, sand or minerals on a surface.

examples.text: Each spring the river floods and [[deposits]] a layer of rich mud that makes the fields fertile.
Hard water [[deposits]] limescale inside your kettle, which is why it turns white over time.
Excess fat is often [[deposited]] around the waist and hips as we get older.

texts: Glaciers [[deposit]] huge rocks far from where they started.
Strong winds can [[deposit]] desert sand on cars hundreds of miles away.
The tides [[deposit]] seaweed and plastic along the beach every morning.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Отложить встречу» — postpone или put off a meeting. Deposit «откладывает» только слой ила, песка или осадка.

collocationTask.prompt: The flood ___ a thick layer of mud in the streets.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Река или наводнение deposit (или leave) слой ила. Place — аккуратно класть, settle — оседать, deliver — доставлять.

nuance.text: The river [[deposits]] fine sand along its banks.
nuance.explanationRu: Deposit — река или вода оставляет осадок: The river deposits sand. Settle — сам осадок оседает: The sand settles at the bottom.

fixIt.text: Every year the river [[postpones]] a thick layer of silt on the surrounding fields.
fixIt.explanationRu: Русское «откладывать» — это и postpone (отложить встречу), и deposit (отложить осадок). О реке и иле — только deposit.

wordFormation.text: Rivers shape the landscape through erosion and [[deposition]].

reply.context: Your flatmate asks: "Why is there white stuff all over the inside of the kettle?"
options: It's limescale. The water round here deposits it every time you boil it.
Calcium carbonate is deposited from the aqueous solution upon heating.
It's limescale. The kettle deposits the water when it gets too hot.
reply.explanationRu: Вода deposit (оставляет) накипь — верно. Чайник не «откладывает воду», а второй ответ звучит как учебник химии, а не разговор с соседом.

rewrite.original: The river left layers of fine sand along its banks.
rewrite.frame: Layers of fine sand ____ along the river's banks.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: sand was deposited, layers were deposited.

definitionEn: to prevent someone from having something they need, or to take it away
situation: Someone is not allowed to have something they need, such as sleep, food, freedom or education.

examples.text: Constant noise from the building site [[deprived]] us of sleep for weeks.
Millions of girls around the world are still [[deprived]] of a basic education.
Cutting the art classes would [[deprive]] students of their only creative outlet.

texts: The long delay [[deprived]] fans of the chance to see the final race.
Children [[deprived]] of affection often struggle to trust adults later.
Without the grant, the village would be [[deprived]] of its only library.

badCollocation.noteRu: Deprive всегда с of: deprive people of their rights. «From» — ошибка по аналогии с prevent from.

collocationTask.prompt: I've been ___ of sleep all week.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Be deprived of sleep — быть лишённым сна, недосыпать. Lack употребляют без of (I lack sleep), а missed и lost так не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Plants [[deprived]] of light soon turn yellow and die.
nuance.explanationRu: Deprive of — лишать необходимого, часто из-за обстоятельств. Deny — отказать в чём-то (решение людей), и без of: denied a visa.

reverse.text: She was [[denied]] a visa because of a mistake on her form.
reverse.explanationRu: Отказать в визе, доступе или праве — deny somebody something. «Deprived a visa» — ошибка: и смысл другой, и нужен был бы предлог of.

fixIt.text: The long drought has [[lost]] farmers of their main source of income.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Лишить кого-то чего-то» — deprive somebody of something. Lose — «лишиться, потерять» самому, конструкции lose somebody of нет.

wordFormation.text: Sleep [[deprivation]] makes it much harder to concentrate at work.

reply.context: A colleague says: "I've been working till two in the morning every night this week."
options: Your sleep deprivation is regrettable and has been duly noted.
No wonder you look exhausted. You've deprived yourself of sleep all week.
Wow, you must feel really deprived of work at the moment.
reply.explanationRu: Deprive yourself of sleep — лишать себя сна, это как раз про коллегу. «Deprived of work» — нехватка работы, а у коллеги её слишком много; первый ответ звучит как официальное письмо.

rewrite.original: The noise outside stopped us from sleeping all night.
rewrite.frame: The noise outside ____ sleep all night.
rewrite.explanationRu: Deprive somebody of something — лишить кого-то чего-то.

definitionEn: the person ranked just below a manager or leader, who replaces them when they are away
senseNote: В некоторых странах deputy — депутат парламента, но главное значение — заместитель: deputy director, deputy head.
situation: You talk about the person who ranks just below the boss and takes over when the boss is absent.

examples.text: When the director is away, her [[deputy]] chairs the weekly meetings.
As [[deputy]], she runs the school whenever the head teacher is away.
The mayor was ill, so his [[deputy]] opened the new bridge instead.

texts: She was promoted to [[deputy]] editor after only two years.
The head of department and her [[deputy]] both interviewed me.
The [[deputy]] manager approved my holiday request this morning.

badCollocation.noteRu: Члена британского парламента называют MP (Member of Parliament). Deputy — прежде всего «заместитель».

collocationTask.prompt: She's the ___ head of our school.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Заместитель директора британской школы — deputy head. Vice бывает в vice-president или vice-chancellor, но не с head; second и under так не говорят.

nuance.text: While the head teacher is on maternity leave, her [[deputy]] is running the school.
nuance.explanationRu: Deputy — заместитель: замещает руководителя и принимает решения. Assistant — помощник, выполняет поручения, но не руководит вместо начальника.

fixIt.text: Please send any urgent questions to the [[substitute]] manager while I'm on holiday.
fixIt.explanationRu: Заместитель руководителя — deputy manager. Substitute — замена (запасной игрок, учитель на один урок), а не должность.

wordFormation.text: I'll [[deputise]] for the director while she is abroad.

reply.context: Your boss emails: "I'll be at a conference all next week. Who should the team go to with problems?"
options: Yo, Maria's gonna be deputy, so chill, it's all good!
I'll be your deputy at the conference, so I'll sit next to you.
Maria can act as your deputy. She knows every project inside out.
reply.explanationRu: Act as someone's deputy — замещать руководителя в его отсутствие. Deputy не значит «сопровождающий», а первый ответ слишком фамильярен для письма начальнику.
